Text Link
People
love
videos.
Everywhere you go, everywhere you scroll, there’s a video waiting.
A video there to educate, entertain, sell, or help. 🤳
And in 2023 and beyond, no one denies that B2B marketing videos are a powerful tool for businesses of any size.

Did you know? 💡

86% of marketers
say video helps them generate leads.

Video is easy to digest, engaging, informative, and, quite frankly, fun!
Here are six popular
B2B videos
for your next marketing campaign. It’s time to blow those quarterly acquisition and revenue targets out of the water! 💥
Best all-rounder video type: B2B explainer videos
Explainer videos — also known as product videos — are a quick, straightforward overview of what you are selling. They’re one of the most frequently used B2B marketing videos.
Here’s a great example of a B2B video:
{lite-youtube videoid="UVNUCBUrHL0" style="background-image: url(' https://img.youtube.com/vi/UVNUCBUrHL0/maxresdefault.jpg '); " }
Product videos touch on your target audience’s pain points, show how your product can help, and highlight a few stand-out features.
They’re a great type of video marketing for you to start with and are usually no longer than 90 seconds. Plus, you have
various production techniques
, such as live-action, animation, vector animation, and talking heads.
Explainer video tips:
Due to the short length of these videos,
move your script quickly
from addressing the problem, introducing your product as the solution, and adding a call to action.
Click here to learn more about writing a great video script.
Don’t skip out on adding humor
if it fits your business. It creates a connection between you and your potential customer.
Put your video front and center;
websites’ landing pages and YouTube are great places to feature it.
Want to learn more about making explainer videos? Check this article:
Improve onboarding & retention: B2B educational videos
Educational videos are the ultimate post-sale experience for your customer. How-to video content includes everything your prospects, leads, and customers need to know about your product or service.

Did you know? 💡

Almost 50% of internet users watched a how-to tutorial video every week. That's why B2B marketing campaigns should always include tutorial content; it gives customers better product knowledge and shows commitment to customer satisfaction.
Here you can find some tips on how to quickly make video tutorials ➔

Educational content provides customer tutorials,
onboarding how-to's
, industry news videos, webinars, or even
employee training videos
.
When dealing with complex features or difficult concepts, it's good to break videos up into
bite-size tutorial videos
.
Check out the learning template below:
{lite-youtube videoid="Zi55FDRnpWs" style="background-image: url(' https://img.youtube.com/vi/Zi55FDRnpWs/hqdefault.jpg '); " }
How-to B2B video marketing can take many different forms; some businesses call them a tutorial library, others a learning academy, and some stick to embedding videos into support documentation.
What to keep in mind when creating B2B educational videos?
Use
screen recordings
so your target audience can follow along.
Use
simple language
in your voiceover and avoid confusing viewers with jargon.
Break up your features into categories
and create a video for each section.
Tackle news topics
that relate to your industry to develop thought-leadership educational content.
Establish your company as an industry leader by hosting
live webinars with Q&A sessions
, and a panel of experts.
When there’s an update to your product’s features, you’ll need to
update your videos.

Tip 💡

Updating a marketing video doesn’t necessarily mean you have to re-record or contract a video production team again. You can easily edit existing videos with an
AI video maker
like Synthesia ➔

Video type best for leads: B2B Product demo videos
A
demo video
is a long-form demonstration or tutorial that details how your product or service works. It is a
visual walkthrough
explaining (not just highlighting) core features and functions in practice.
A marketing video that demos a product runs between 10 and 30 minutes long and is often filmed in a webinar format. They’re great if your current target market struggles to understand how your product works under the hood.
Easiest video type: B2B customer testimonial videos
Customer testimonial videos are the new word of mouth.
It’s one thing to tell people how great you are, but when other people sing your praises… that’s gold for your marketing strategy! 🥰
A video testimonial gives your viewers an unbiased and unscripted review of the results you’ve achieved for a customer.
You can gain your target audience’s trust through customer testimonials, highlight what you offer, and get the edge over your competitors. It fits perfectly into the lifecycle of any B2B company during the
consideration or decision-making stage
.
3 ways to get video testimonials for B2B marketing
1️⃣ Initiate the
request for a testimonial
over email or after you have received positive feedback.
2️⃣ Schedule a
formal shoot
with customers to create videos
OR do a
video call
to record the testimonial interview style.
OR invite your
customers to record themselves
and send the video to you.
3️⃣ You can also source
written testimonials from the internet
, for example, Google or Facebook, and use it as additional footage or voiceover in a testimonial montage.
Here's an example of a testimonial video:
{lite-youtube videoid="FCNKoXavf4A" style="background-image: url(' https://img.youtube.com/vi/FCNKoXavf4A/hqdefault.jpg '); " }
Most underrated video type: B2B brand videos
A brand video shows your
company’s values and mission
. It details the inner workings of your team, makes your brand more human, and is designed to make the viewer feel like they know who you are.
This type of B2B video does well on the about page of your website or on social media platforms. It can:
Build trust
with new visitors and customers
Attract investors
and employees with the health of your company culture
Convince top talent
that your company is fantastic to work for.
Best video type to win trust: B2B case study videos
Case studies for your business are like customer testimonials fitted with a turbo engine!
Case study videos take this general format:
The initial
reason

why
your customer chose your company
The
services they used
to resolve their problem
How
the services work out in practice
The long-tail
results
related to revenue or a similar KPI
When your customer isn’t speaking, case studies are often narrated or supported with title slides and
statistics
. You can even include screen recordings and photos:
{lite-youtube videoid="8X6ZJOEu8ps" style="background-image: url(' https://img.youtube.com/vi/8X6ZJOEu8ps/maxresdefault.jpg '); " }

Benefits of Employee Training: 6 Measurable Outcomes
Written by
Kevin Alster
February 26, 2026
Create engaging training videos in 160+ languages.
Get started for FREE
In this article
Text Link
Most organizations say they care about development. Far fewer build sustainable pathways for
skill development, career advancement, and internal mobility.
LinkedIn’s
Workplace Learning Report 2025

shows how wide the gap is:
36%
of organizations lead as “career development champions,”
31%
lag with limited adoption, and
33%
are at the starting line, with minimal or no career development initiatives.
That gap matters because development isn’t a program. It’s a company-wide capability that shapes how organizations:
Attract and retain
in-demand talent
Prepare teams for constant change
Build internal mobility
when external hiring is constrained
Sustain performance
as roles evolve
Closing the gap takes shared ownership. Leadership sets priorities and funds capability building. Managers translate learning into coaching and reinforcement. Learning and development builds pathways and measurement. Employees pull support in the flow of work and signal where they want to grow.
In this guide, we’ll focus on six outcomes L&D leaders can measure and improve. For each one, we’ll cover what it looks like and the levers that make it scalable, including formal programs and internal mobility.

What are you trying to improve?

Choose a goal to jump to the section you need.

⏱️
Faster ramp → Time-to-competency

🛡️
Fewer mistakes → Execution quality

⚡
More throughput → Operational efficiency

🌱
Better retention → Engagement and intent to stay

🗺️
More lateral moves → Internal mobility

🔄
Faster adoption → Change readiness

6 outcomes to measure and improve
Start with what needs to change on the job. Then design the mix that gets you there: role paths, manager reinforcement, and mobility options employees can access. Use the outcomes below as your measurement backbone, then tune the levers until results hold across teams and regions.
1. Time-to-competency
Why it matters
Ramp time is expensive. When competency takes too long, managers compensate with extra oversight and peers become the help desk. Shortening time-to-competency stabilizes performance and improves the employee experience.
What to measure
Time to hit role competency milestones (scorecards, observed checklists, QA rubrics)
30/60/90-day competency reviews (manager rating plus employee self-assessment)
First-pass quality on critical tasks and rework rates
Levers that scale
Define competency in observable terms by role and level
Map learning to milestones and real tasks
Reinforce with job aids and searchable guidance in the flow of work
Give managers a simple coaching cadence with prompts and checklists
Quick wins
Pick 3–5 competencies per role, write clear criteria, then add a 30/60/90 checkpoint that produces a single “ready/not yet” signal.
🎥 Where Synthesia can help
‍
Create short role walkthroughs that show “what good looks like” so
onboarding
stays consistent across teams and locations.
2. Execution quality and error reduction
Why it matters
Quality problems spread. One unclear standard becomes ten workarounds. Training improves quality when it targets the decision point where errors happen and reinforces the right behavior before drift sets in.
What to measure
Defect rates, rework, policy exceptions
QA scores and variation across teams, shifts, and regions
Escalations, audit findings, and repeat issue categories
Levers that scale
Establish a single source of truth for critical processes
Trigger refreshers after incidents and process changes
Use role-specific examples, including edge cases
Add lightweight verification (spot checks, observation, QA sampling)
Quick wins
Take the top three error drivers. For each one, publish a one-page job aid and a two-minute refresher focused on the step where the mistake occurs.
🎥 Where Synthesia can help
Turn common failure modes into
quick visual refreshers
that standardize the correct method across regions.
3. Operational efficiency and productivity
Why it matters
When knowledge lives in inboxes and meetings, output depends on who is available to explain it. Efficient teams reduce repeat questions and protect SME time by making answers easy to find and easy to trust.
What to measure
Cycle time, handle time, throughput, backlog (role-dependent)
SME hours spent repeating training or answering the same questions
“How do I…?” ticket volume and duplicate work indicators
Levers that scale
Convert repeat questions into reusable modules and job aids
Improve findability where work happens (tools, knowledge base, intranet)
Set an update cadence with clear ownership
Standardize onboarding and refreshers for high-volume roles
Quick wins
List the ten most repeated questions from new hires. Build a searchable starter kit that answers each in one screen and links to the official process.
🎥 Where Synthesia can help
Publish
micro-videos
for tool flows and common questions so employees can self-serve without waiting on SMEs.
4. Engagement and intent to stay
Why it matters
Development is now a baseline expectation, not a perk. When growth feels random or inaccessible, engagement drops and attrition risk rises. Evidence links access to development opportunities with higher intention to stay, and that relationship may be stronger for Gen Z workers in some contexts.

What the research says about retention

Development access is linked to retention.
A 2023 systematic review found continuing professional development/training is associated with higher intention to stay and lower turnover intention, with one included study suggesting a stronger effect for younger workers in that context.

[Source]

Perception drives impact.
Research on perceived investment in employee development links it to lower turnover intention through mechanisms such as affective commitment and employability perceptions, which means access alone isn’t enough if employees don’t experience it as real.

[Source]

What to measure
Engagement items tied to growth (career support, learning access, manager coaching)
Participation in development activities, segmented by role and tenure
Retention and attrition for critical roles and high performers
Signals of interest in growth (internal applications, mentoring, project bids)
Levers that scale
Make pathways visible and specific to roles
Support manager-led career conversations with structure
Offer flexible options beyond courses (projects, coaching, mentoring)
Recognize managers who develop talent and enable mobility
Quick wins
Roll out a quarterly manager template for career check-ins. Keep it short. Require one documented next step per employee.
🎥 Where Synthesia can help
‍
Share consistent messaging on growth and mobility so employees understand what development looks like in your organization.
5. Internal mobility and career progression
Why it matters
Mobility turns learning into opportunity. It also reduces dependency on external hiring. Promotions matter, but lateral moves often keep critical talent engaged while building new capabilities.
What to measure
Internal fill rate for priority roles
Lateral moves, rotations, shadowing participation
Time-in-role to move and promotion rates by function
Talent marketplace activity (applications, project matching, skills profiles)
Levers that scale
Define lateral pathways when upward moves are limited
Create “try it” options with clear timeboxes (shadowing, short rotations, gigs)
Set governance for fairness and transparency
Train managers to develop talent without hoarding it
Quick wins
Run a 30-day shadowing pilot in one function. Limit the scope, set learning goals, collect manager feedback, and publish a short playbook based on results.
🎥 Where Synthesia can help
‍
Create role preview videos that clarify expectations and skills so employees can choose pathways with confidence.
6. Change readiness and capability agility
Why it matters
Work changes faster than curricula. When enablement lags, adoption slows and performance drops. High readiness means people understand what changed and what to do next, with minimal disruption.
What to measure
Adoption by role (usage, compliance, feature utilization)
Time-to-adoption and backsliding rates after rollout
Change-related incidents, exceptions, and support load
Understanding checks for change-critical updates
Levers that scale
Break change enablement into role-specific modules with clear actions
Provide manager toolkits that support reinforcement
Localize where required and keep updates simple to ship
Build a reinforcement loop (checkpoints, nudges, validation)
Quick wins
For the next major change, publish a “3 actions to take now” update by role and schedule a one-week reinforcement checkpoint with managers.
🎥 Where Synthesia can help
‍
Ship short
change updates
that teams can absorb quickly and share consistently.
How to achieve these outcomes
Outcomes improve when development works as an operating system. It needs to show up in hiring, onboarding, performance conversations, and mobility decisions. Otherwise, learning stays separate from the work it is meant to improve.
The system has to run in two directions. Leadership creates the conditions for growth. Employees need clear ways to use what is available. When either side is missing, development becomes uneven. High performers find a path. Everyone else is left to improvise.
Start with shared ownership
Leadership sets capability priorities, protects time, and funds the work. That includes manager enablement and mobility mechanisms that still function when the business is under pressure.
Managers make development visible. They connect learning to standards, create room for practice, and give feedback that turns knowledge into competence. They also sponsor people for opportunities instead of holding them back.
L&D, Enablement, and HR build pathways and remove friction. They translate priorities into role-based plans, equip managers with tools they will use, and keep measurement consistent across teams.
Employees bring agency. They pull learning when they need it and raise a hand for projects, shadowing, and rotations.
Make human-guided learning non-negotiable
Courses can build knowledge. Judgment grows through practice, feedback, and context. People learn faster when they can watch someone do the work, try it themselves, then refine.
Build person-guided experiences into your pathways:
Career champions who open doors and advocate for talent
Mentors who share patterns and decision-making
Peer learning through shadowing, cohort practice, and communities of practice
These experiences also make development feel real. That matters for engagement and retention.
Use multiple learning modalities on purpose
Different outcomes respond to different modalities. Choose the lightest approach that still changes behavior. Add guided practice where work is complex or risk is high.
Modalities to combine:
Manager-led coaching tied to observable standards
Mentoring and sponsorship that supports progression and mobility
Peer learning through shadowing and collaborative practice
Performance support such as job aids, checklists, and searchable guidance
Formal learning paths for onboarding, reskilling, leadership, and compliance
Treat mobility as part of the learning system
Mobility converts learning into opportunity. It also protects retention when promotions are limited. Lateral moves, rotations, and shadowing keep growth moving without requiring a title change.
Mobility needs structure. Define pathways. Set criteria. Make expectations easy to understand. Track internal fill rates and lateral movement, not only promotions.
🎥
Where Synthesia can help
‍
Video training is useful when demonstration and consistency matter. Use it to show “what good looks like,” support managers with reusable coaching moments, and keep guidance current as processes change. Keep videos short, then tie them to a pathway, a checklist, or a role milestone so they stay connected to outcomes.
Next Steps
If getting this right feels hard, that’s normal. Development sits at the intersection of business priorities, manager capacity, and employee needs. Any step forward is better than waiting for the perfect program.
When in doubt, ask your employees where support would make the biggest difference. Focus on what gets in their way today: the skills they need to do their job well, the moments they feel stuck, and the opportunities they want access to next. Use those signals to choose one outcome from this guide, run a small pilot, and improve from there.

faq
Frequently asked questions
What are the benefits of employee training?
Employee training improves measurable outcomes like time-to-proficiency, quality, productivity, engagement, retention, and readiness for change. The biggest gains come when training is consistent, role-based, and designed to scale across teams.
What training outcomes should L&D leaders measure?
Start with leading indicators (completion, assessment scores, confidence, manager validation, time-to-proficiency) and pair them with business outcomes (quality metrics, error rates, customer metrics, productivity, retention). Choose measures tied to the behaviors training is meant to change.
How do you measure time-to-proficiency?
Define what “proficient” means for a role (tasks, quality thresholds, speed), then track how quickly employees reach that standard after onboarding or training. Manager checklists, QA rubrics, and performance dashboards work well.
How does training improve employee retention?
Training supports retention by increasing role clarity, confidence, and growth opportunities. It can also reduce frustration from unclear processes and inconsistent guidance, which often drives attrition.
What’s the best way to scale employee training across regions and roles?
Standardize the core curriculum, modularize content by role, and set governance for accuracy, approvals, and update cadence. Use formats that are easy to refresh and localize so training stays aligned with real work.

9 Vital Benefits of Security Awareness Training
Written by
Kevin Alster
June 10, 2024
Create AI videos with 240+ avatars in 160+ languages.
Try Free AI Video
Get started for FREE
In this article
Text Link
Your organization's security is only as strong as the training that your newest intern received.
That's pretty terrifying if security awareness training isn't part of your usual modus operandi!
Trained employees are the ultimate first line of defense. With the right protocols and training programs, you can turn your biggest weakness (people) into your biggest strength. Your employees are the key to stopping issues long before they spiral into the latest data scandal on the evening news.
(And if that wasn't enough, research shows it can cost your company up to 2.7 times more not to meet compliance standards!)
Here's why security awareness training is essential for boosting your business's defense against cyber attacks 👇.
What is security awareness training?
Security awareness training is a continuous
process of educating employees about information security
. The internet evolves quickly, and so do scams. Even the most savvy Gen Z might fall victim to a malware attack if they aren't aware of what's out there.
Promoting security awareness means keeping up with hacker tactics, updating employees on current threats, and reminding them of recent pitfalls that other companies have fallen into.
A solid security awareness training program equips employees with the knowledge and skills to protect organizational assets from cyber threats. The activities within such security awareness training programs can be:
Led by an instructor in a classroom setting, workshop, or group discussion
Online, as a webinar or
e-learning modules
Printed as posters, flyers, handbooks, guides
Phishing simulations
Practical cyber attack drills
Instructional videos or animations
Quizzes, challenges, games
What topics should security awareness training cover?
The most common topics discussed in a security awareness program include phishing and social engineering attacks, password security and management, data protection and privacy, antivirus software, types of security threats and malware (especially phishing scams), security threats reporting and response, and remote work security.
The importance of security awareness
Preventing cyberattacks is easier than fixing their damage. In 2023, two Danish hosting providers
lost all customer data
to a ransomware attack and had to shut down. Similarly, 23andMe faced a major data breach affecting 6.9 million users, resulting in multiple
class action lawsuits
. Then, there's the notorious 2015 Ashley Madison hack that publicly outed millions of men for cheating activity, as described in Netflix's recent docuseries.
These aren't isolated incidents. Vulnerabilities rise by
25%
each year, and the annual average cost of cybercrime is
predicted
to exceed $23 trillion by 2027, up from $8.4 trillion in 2022.
Ignoring the importance of cybersecurity training and its impact on security awareness can lead to lost deals, damaged reputation, fines, and high recovery costs. Investing in security awareness training helps reverse these effects. And it doesn't even have to be expensive, with the rise of AI facilitating the rapid scaling of
security training videos
.
Did you know? 🤔

The right training brings major benefits. Business leaders say that thanks to improved security defense, the percentage of deals lost due to perceived inadequacies in a company's cybersecurity posture
dropped
from 67% to 38% in a year.

1. You set standard guidelines that reduce the risk of human error
88%
of security breaches are caused by employee mistakes, which can be avoided with proper security awareness training. Robust defense systems are crucial, but the human element is the first line of defense, and it's critical that all your employees understand:
Who is at risk
Why and when they might fall prey to a cyberattack
Common types of attacks
When cybersecurity threats are likely to occur
So everyone, not just IT teams, needs cybersecurity awareness training. With such a program, you can set standard guidelines that improve cybersecurity awareness and reduce the risk of human errors.
Not sure where to begin with security awareness training at your company? Start teaching employees general notions related to security risks and introduce your company guidelines, security protocols, and security practices, like in
this example
:
{lite-youtube videoid="x1hYRR9YVLo" style="background-image: url('https://img.youtube.com/vi/x1hYRR9YVLo/hqdefault.jpg');" }
2. Your routine training prevents data vulnerability
Cybersecurity training helps protect sensitive information, minimize risk, and even prevent data breaches. That's why, with phishing attacks alone,
80%
of organizations noticed that their security awareness training program made their employees more vigilant about the peril and less vulnerable to this threat.
Once employees get proper training to recognize phishing attempts, they're significantly better equipped to navigate potential risks and will be less likely to fall victim to a phishing email.
This means you must equip your staff with the knowledge to identify and respond to various cyber threats and keep them up to date with the latest in the threat landscape.
Did you know? 🤔

The average security training program had a
37-fold ROI
, and even the least effective programs had a 7-fold ROI.

Here's an
example
of a prevention training video you could create for your company:
{lite-youtube videoid="tVSRi6gPfeo" style="background-image: url('https://img.youtube.com/vi/tVSRi6gPfeo/hqdefault.jpg');" }
3. Your "Security posture" across all departments improves significantly
Security posture is a comprehensive overview of your organization's security health, significantly improves when all employees are aware and play their part in protecting your company.
Think of your company as a castle with many access points. A strong security awareness program trains everyone to keep the castle safe and spot sneaky attackers.
Did you know? 🤔

46%
of all cyber breaches are reported at companies with less than 1,000 employees.

Here's how to make security a shared responsibility:
Name a security champion:
Appoint a security champion for each department to address questions and concerns.
Provide regular training:
Create and regularly update security training programs and materials.
For more insights, check out this video:
{lite-youtube videoid="dnAizGuxbbM" style="background-image: url('https://img.youtube.com/vi/dnAizGuxbbM/hqdefault.jpg');" }
4. You're always compliant with industry regulations and standards
Non-compliance can be very costly. A McKinsey survey found that
40%
of customers stopped buying from a company after a security breach. Additionally, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) says that even a less severe violation could
cost
a company either 2% of its worldwide annual revenue or €10 million, whichever is more.
Security training brings you closer to compliance, making your employees aware of regulations and more capable of following them closely.
To ease your compliance efforts, automate regulatory change monitoring with AI and receive alerts when relevant laws are updated. Thomson Reuters Regulatory Intelligence (TRRI) is a great tool if you need help to ensure compliance with industry standards.
5. Awareness speeds up response to security incidents
Knowing how to act in a crisis makes all the difference. Yet only
45%
of companies have an incident response plan. When you invest in security training, you will:
Reduce response time during a security incident
Improve coordination among team members or departments
Minimize the impact on business operations
As you create training content on how to respond in case of an incident and develop your response plan, make sure to include essential metrics like mean time to detect, mean time to acknowledge, mean time to recovery, etc.

this exact template
for your team:

6. Protect sensitive data with employee password management
Weak passwords are a common cause of data breaches, with
30%
of internet users experiencing security incidents because of cracked passwords. Once a password has been cracked, hackers can steal sensitive data and either hold you or your employees at ransom or simply sell it on the
dark web
.
One of the benefits of security awareness training videos like the one below is that they can help your employees understand exactly how hackers break into accounts:
{lite-youtube videoid="YiRPt4vrSSw" style="background-image: url('https://img.youtube.com/vi/YiRPt4vrSSw/hqdefault.jpg');" }
Security awareness training and educating employees on password best practices make it harder for hackers to steal your data. Employees who are aware of this danger will also:
Understand how important it is to handle sensitive information with care.
Know better than to set their passwords as 123456 (the most commonly used password by worldwide internet users and used by thousands of users in the Ashley Madison hack!)
Use multi-factor authentication for extra protection.
Here's an
example
of effective security awareness training to teach your employees how to protect sensitive data:

7. Your security culture is positive (not annoying)
A positive security culture includes the ideas, customs, and behaviors that influence your organization's security approach. It defines how your company prioritizes security.
According to KnowBe4, organizations can reach five maturity levels in fostering a security awareness training culture, from basic compliance (Level 1) to a sustainable security culture (Level 5). The latter involves intentional programs that measure, shape, and reinforce security culture through various methods.

The 5 levels of security culture that an organization can achieve (

)

With a strong security culture, you instill accountability and avoid cyber threats, helping everyone understand their role in keeping data safe and avoiding breaches. It encourages open communication about potential security issues, leading to faster response times and improving your company's reputation with clients, partners, and stakeholders.
Here's what Microsoft says about creating a security culture in business — "
No piece of software will ever stop quite so many attacks as a workforce that is trained to spot and avoid threats.
"
{lite-youtube videoid="fST4hrEq3FA" style="background-image: url('https://img.youtube.com/vi/fST4hrEq3FA/hqdefault.jpg');" }
8. You maintain a gold standard of employee safety and wellbeing
The security knowledge employees gain from training helps them protect personal data and navigate the web responsibly, even outside of work. Understanding phishing, malware, and other threats can prevent identity theft and financial fraud, reducing people's anxiety and improving mental well-being.
But this benefit extends to your security team, who's constantly under a lot of stress, and to those who develop awareness training for your employees. These people care a lot about preventing breaches, passing on knowledge, and enabling everyone to protect the company.
The more quality security training you provide, the more awareness, security measures, protection, and peace of mind you will increase across all teams and departments.
Did you know? 🤔

65%
of Chief Information Security Officers say work-related stress affects their ability to protect the organization. Offer your CISOs and IT experts dedicated mental health support.

9. You earn consumers' trust
For
79%
of consumers, data protection is the most important factor in trusting a company — more important than fast customer service or consistent experiences.
Indeed, people buy from those they know, like, and trust. By showing potential buyers that you value their data privacy and that everyone at your company is trained to protect it, you're more likely to earn their trust.
Of course, you must also let customers know about your efforts. Publicly share your commitment to cybersecurity. Turn these efforts into a marketing asset by highlighting your security training initiatives whenever you have the opportunity to communicate about them.
Create engaging and scalable security awareness training with AI
You've seen the benefits of cyber security training and how it can massively improve awareness and protection. The easiest way to create such impactful security training is with video.
AI videos are quick to create and scale, customizable for any language and culture, and accessible to global employees. Plus, they allow remote workers to learn asynchronously, increasing retention and application of the information.

makes it easier and more scalable with minimal resources.

1. Synthesia
URL:
https://www.synthesia.io/
What is Synthesia?
I tested Synthesia on the Enterprise plan in February 2026. It positions itself as a complete AI video platform for enterprise teams, and that positioning felt accurate during my hands-on use.
The platform is clearly built for structured corporate workflows: training content, HR communication, sales enablement, and multilingual business messaging. The interface is slide-based and presentation-oriented. The workflow is straightforward: write the script, choose an avatar, select a voice, adjust layout, generate, and translate if needed.
One important limitation I encountered: the platform only supports Chrome and Edge. Safari is not supported.
How realistic are Synthesia’s avatars?
In English, avatar realism was very strong. Facial animation, micro-expressions, eye contact, and hand gestures felt natural and controlled. Lip-sync was precise, even in longer sentences.
Minor facial artifacts can appear on close inspection, but overall English output is among the strongest I’ve tested.
In Spanish, realism remained high but slightly lower than English. Lip-sync stayed accurate, though I noticed small micro-misalignments around the lips and occasional minor hand or finger inconsistencies.
How expressive and natural are the avatars?
The avatars are expressive within a professional range. Gestures are measured and appropriate for corporate communication. Head movement is subtle and structured.
This makes the platform well suited for formal presentations, internal training, and B2B communication. It is not designed for highly animated or dramatic performance styles.
How good are the voices and lip-sync?
Voice quality was excellent in English. Pacing and intonation sounded natural, and delivery felt close to human in tone.
New features such as speech regeneration per paragraph and adjustable voice speed add useful control.
Lip-sync performance was consistently precise. Long sentences remained stable without visible drift.
In Spanish, voice naturalness was slightly reduced compared to English, but pacing and synchronization remained solid. Rendering time for translation was significantly longer than English.
How strong is localization and multilingual support?
Localization is one of Synthesia’s strongest areas.
It supports generation in 160+ languages and translation into 139 languages while preserving the original voice identity. Voice cloning is available in 29 languages.
The translation workflow is fully integrated inside the editor. I did not need to use a separate tool. In my Spanish test, speech pacing was preserved and lip-sync remained accurate. Dialect options are available.
The only drawback is rendering speed. My Spanish version took noticeably longer to generate than the English one.
What use cases does Synthesia excel at?
Based on my testing, Synthesia performs best in:
Enterprise training
HR communication
Sales enablement content
Structured multilingual corporate videos
The structured slide-based system and strong in-editor translation make it particularly effective for large organizations producing content in multiple languages.
What use cases does Synthesia struggle with?
Synthesia is less suitable for:
Automation-heavy workflows
Rapid marketing iteration
Highly expressive or cinematic storytelling
Projects requiring event-triggered automation
There is no automation system comparable to a “Video Agent.” Rendering times are also slower than some competitors.
What are Synthesia’s strengths?
From my hands-on testing:
Highly realistic English avatars
Strong and seamless in-editor translation workflow
Stable and precise lip-sync
Enterprise-grade collaboration and publishing features
AI Playground for advanced image and video generation
Voice regeneration and pacing control
What are Synthesia’s weaknesses?
No Safari support
Slower rendering times
No automation equivalent to a Video Agent
Slight realism drop in translated versions
How does Synthesia compare to other AI avatar generators?
Synthesia stands out for corporate realism and structured presentation workflows. It prioritizes controlled, professional delivery and multilingual scalability.
It is less focused on automation-driven personalization or advertising performance.
How does Synthesia compare to HeyGen?
In my testing:
Synthesia’s English realism was slightly stronger.
Translation workflow was more seamless because it is fully integrated in the editor.
HeyGen rendered faster.
HeyGen offers automation via Video Agent.
HeyGen feels more flexible for dynamic workflows.
Synthesia is more presentation-oriented. HeyGen is faster and more automation-driven.
How does Synthesia compare to Colossyan?
Both use slide-based systems.
Synthesia delivered higher avatar realism and stronger emotional alignment.
Translation quality felt more polished in Synthesia.
Colossyan emphasizes SCORM and structured learning workflows.
If realism and multilingual quality are the priority, I would choose Synthesia. If SCORM-focused LMS workflows dominate, Colossyan has advantages.
How does Synthesia compare to DeepBrain AI Studios?
Synthesia offers a more structured and presentation-driven experience.
DeepBrain provides broader ecosystem integration and manual gesture control.
Synthesia’s English realism felt slightly more natural.
DeepBrain integrates more advanced AI video models directly.
Synthesia feels optimized for enterprise presentation. DeepBrain feels like a larger technical production ecosystem.
What is the verdict on Synthesia?
From my February 2026 testing, Synthesia is one of the strongest enterprise-focused AI avatar platforms available.
If your priority is highly realistic English avatars, seamless multilingual translation, and structured corporate production, it performs extremely well.
If you need faster iteration, automation-driven workflows, or marketing-focused agility, other platforms may be a better fit.
2. Creatify
URL:
https://creatify.ai/
What is Creatify?
I tested Creatify in February 2026 on the free, credit-based plan. It has evolved far beyond a simple UGC avatar generator. The positioning is clear: this is an AI advertising platform built for performance marketing.
The workflow reflects that focus. Instead of building a presentation-style video, I moved through an ad production pipeline:
URL / script / image → choose avatar & style → generate variations → analyze performance → launch campaign.
Creatify supports script-to-video, URL-to-video, product-to-video, image-to-video, and batch ad generation. It also integrates built-in A/B testing, analytics (ROAS, CTR, spend tracking), and direct social publishing. This is a conversion-focused system, not a corporate presentation tool.
How realistic are Creatify’s avatars?
Avatar realism was extremely high in my test.
Creatify offers 1500+ avatars and uses its proprietary Aurora model for image-to-video avatar generation. Full-body expressiveness is supported, and emotional realism is strong, especially in UGC-style formats.
In my English script test (about 100 words), the result was one of the most realistic UGC-style avatars I’ve tested. The performance felt natural and optimized for ad environments rather than corporate presentations.
How expressive and natural are the avatars?
Expressiveness is one of Creatify’s strongest areas.
The avatars demonstrate:
Full-body motion
Context-aware gestures
Natural head movement
Emotion-aware lip-sync
20+ emotional presets (on selected avatars)
Gestures felt aligned with speech rhythm, and the overall delivery was optimized for authenticity in social ad formats. Compared to corporate-oriented tools, the performance felt more dynamic and conversion-driven.
How good are the voices and lip-sync?
Lip-sync performance was very stable. It reacted emotionally and aligned well with speech rhythm.
Creatify supports 140+ AI voice characters and integrates with ElevenLabs for higher-quality voice output. Voice realism depends on the engine selected. With stronger engines, realism improves significantly.
In my Spanish test, manual translation was required. After translation, lip-sync remained precise and gesture alignment stayed consistent across languages. There is no automatic translation system inside the platform.
How strong is localization and multilingual support?
Creatify supports multilingual voice generation, but it does not include automatic script translation. I had to create the Spanish version manually.
Once translated, performance quality remained strong. Lip-sync stayed accurate, and emotional delivery was preserved.
However, compared to platforms with built-in translation workflows, the process is less streamlined for multilingual scaling.
What use cases does Creatify excel at?
Based on my testing, Creatify performs best in:
E-commerce advertising
Performance marketing campaigns
TikTok and Meta ads
High-volume creative testing
Batch variation workflows
The built-in A/B testing, analytics dashboard, and direct campaign launch integrations make it highly suitable for growth teams.
What use cases does Creatify struggle with?
Creatify is less suitable for:
Corporate training
Structured HR communication
Long-form internal presentations
Slide-based multilingual enterprise production
The system is optimized for ad performance, not structured corporate storytelling.
What are Creatify’s strengths?
From my hands-on testing:
Extremely realistic UGC avatars
Proprietary Aurora avatar engine
Full-body expressive motion
Batch ad variation creation
Built-in performance analytics
Direct ad deployment integration
AI music generation
Strong ecosystem of AI models
What are Creatify’s weaknesses?
No built-in automatic translation
Credit-based pricing complexity
Vertical-first ad mindset
Less suited for structured corporate workflows
How does Creatify compare to other AI avatar generators?
Creatify operates in a different category compared to corporate avatar platforms. Its strength is measurable advertising performance rather than structured presentation design.
How does Creatify compare to HeyGen?
In my testing:
Creatify delivered stronger UGC-style realism for ads.
Creatify includes campaign analytics and direct ad launch tools.
HeyGen is more structured and presentation-driven.
HeyGen offers built-in multilingual translation.
Creatify fits performance marketing pipelines. HeyGen fits corporate communication workflows.
How does Creatify compare to Synthesia?
Creatify focuses on advertising scale and variation testing.
Synthesia focuses on enterprise presentation and multilingual training.
Synthesia provides seamless in-editor translation.
Creatify requires manual translation.
If the goal is structured multilingual corporate content, Synthesia is stronger. For scalable ad production and testing, Creatify is more suitable.
How does Creatify compare to InVideo?
Creatify provides persistent, high-quality avatar performance.
InVideo relies on agent-based automation and does not offer persistent digital twins.
Creatify’s lip-sync and emotional realism are stronger.
InVideo integrates a broader range of generative models but with less avatar control.
Creatify offers more controlled avatar realism for ads. InVideo emphasizes automated video generation pipelines.
What is the verdict on Creatify?
From my February 2026 testing, Creatify is one of the strongest platforms available for AI-driven advertising.
If your goal is scalable ad production, emotionally expressive UGC-style avatars, batch variation testing, and direct performance tracking, it performs exceptionally well.
If you need structured enterprise communication or seamless multilingual translation inside a slide-based workflow, other platforms are better suited.
3. Heygen
URL:
https://www.heygen.com/
What is HeyGen?
I tested HeyGen in February 2026 on the free 720p plan, and compared to my previous test in November, the platform has matured significantly. It no longer feels like just an avatar tool. It feels like a structured video production ecosystem built for creators, marketers, and business teams.
Several updates were immediately noticeable during testing. The script panel has been rebuilt with a cleaner single-input layout, inline pause controls, pronunciation glossary management, and formatting preservation when pasting scripts. Avatar creation has been reduced to roughly 15 seconds using a single webcam recording that captures appearance, voice, motion, and consent. The new Avatar 4 engine is now the default expressive model, offering higher realism, while an “Unlimited Avatar” option exists for cost control.
The workflow is straightforward and intuitive: write the script, choose an avatar, select a voice, customize layout, generate, and export. My 100-word script rendered in 30 seconds, which is a dramatic speed improvement compared to earlier tests.
How realistic are HeyGen’s avatars?
Avatar realism is one of the strongest aspects of HeyGen. During my hands-on test, I observed subtle micro-movements in the shoulders and torso, natural blinking, controlled posture shifts, and realistic hand gestures. Hair physics and hand behavior, which are often weak points in AI avatars, were handled impressively.
Lip-sync was technically accurate. Mouth movements aligned precisely with speech, even in longer sentences. On very close inspection, lip texture can still reveal slight synthetic characteristics, but in standard viewing conditions the illusion holds up well.
Overall, realism approached real presenter quality in several moments, especially in English.
How expressive and natural are the avatars?
Expressiveness is where HeyGen stands out most. Movements feel intentional rather than pre-programmed. Gestures align naturally with speech rhythm, and head movement is subtle but responsive. The avatars do not feel rigid or slide-based. Instead, they carry a fluid on-screen presence.
The Avatar 4 engine noticeably improves emotional nuance compared to previous versions. Delivery feels more human and context-aware rather than mechanically timed.
Compared to more structured corporate platforms, HeyGen feels more dynamic and visually engaging.
How good are the voices and lip-sync?
The voice ecosystem is deep and flexible. HeyGen integrates ElevenLabs, ElevenLabs 3, and Panda engines. Beyond simple text-to-speech, it offers tools such as Direct Voice (describe tone or emotion), Mirror Voice (match your own delivery), and Auto-enhance for pacing and emotional tagging.
In my testing, voice delivery was expressive and natural. Tone presets such as Professional and Lifestyle provide quick stylistic adjustments. Lip-sync remained accurate in both English and Spanish, with stable articulation even in longer phrases.
The Voice Doctor feature is particularly useful. I could describe an issue with delivery in chat, hear improved variations, and save the refined version. That level of post-generation control adds a layer of quality assurance not commonly found in competing tools.
How strong is localization and multilingual support?
HeyGen supports generation and translation in over 70 languages and 175+ dialects. I tested Spanish localization using the dubbing workflow. Speech pacing was preserved, and the faster natural rhythm of Spanish was reflected appropriately. Lip-sync remained accurate, and the improvements in hair and hand realism carried over into the translated version.
The main drawback is workflow structure. Translation requires a separate dubbing process rather than a one-click in-editor translation. It works well, but it is not as seamless as fully integrated systems in some other platforms.
What use cases does HeyGen excel at?
Based on my testing, HeyGen performs best in:
Expressive marketing videos
Brand storytelling
Internal business communication
Podcast translation
Social media content
Scalable professional video production
What use cases does HeyGen struggle with?
HeyGen is less suited for:
Ultra-cinematic productions requiring granular manual animation control
Highly structured SCORM-focused LMS production
What are HeyGen’s strengths?
Industry-leading expressiveness
Strong micro-movement and gesture realism
Powerful voice ecosystem
Very fast rendering
Clean and intuitive UI
Video Agent automation
Broad business integrations
What are HeyGen’s weaknesses?
Translation requires a separate workflow

InVideo does offer AI-generated presenter assets, but they do not feel as central or refined as in dedicated avatar studios. Avatars generated through the AI agent look serviceable at 720p/1080p — lip-sync is roughly aligned, and facial motion responds adequately to the underlying audio. However, the output does not reach the level of realism seen in top-tier avatar platforms.
Movement ranges from steady to slightly stiff, and gestures are functional rather than nuanced. Hand visibility is limited or inconsistent. In many cases, scenes end up feeling like
illustrated presenters
embedded inside broader timeline edits rather than fully dynamic avatars.
How expressive and natural are the avatars?
Expressiveness was generally modest. When testing spoken content, the facial motion and head shifts were present, but gestures and emotional nuance felt flat. The agent translates intent into a video structure that prioritizes clarity over performance subtlety, which works well for explainer and informational video formats but lacks the fluid expressiveness of platforms like HeyGen.
Because avatar generation in InVideo is tied into a broader automated pipeline, individual motion refinement isn’t accessible at a granular level. You cannot fine-tune gestures or body language independently; the system focuses on
scene pacing and compositional flow
rather than avatar performance nuance.
How good are the voices and lip-sync?
Lip-sync accuracy is acceptable for general use: mouth movements align with generated narration and imported speech tracks without dramatic drift. Voice quality, however, remains functional. TTS output tends toward neutral cadence and lacks the emotional coloring present in dedicated voice engines such as ElevenLabs.
In longer speech segments I tested, rhythm and pacing were stable, but inflection and energy were limited. There are no deep voice editing features or tone controls. InVideo’s workflow is designed to generate a complete video rather than let you customize vocal performance at a detailed level.
How strong is localization and multilingual support?
InVideo supports text input in multiple languages, and the AI agent can generate translated narration if you instruct it manually. However, there is no built-in or automatic multilingual workflow; translation has to be handled as a separate script prompt or external translation step before generating video output.
Multilingual lip-sync is technically accurate once imported, but InVideo does not offer in-editor translation tools or localized voice cloning options. This makes localization possible but
not seamless
compared to platforms with integrated translation pipelines.
What use cases does InVideo excel at?
Based on my testing, InVideo performs best in:
Creative video automation
Social media content workflows
Timeline-driven editing with AI assistance
Repurposing long content into short clips
Narrated explainers and marketing assets
Hybrid generative/manual video creation
What use cases does InVideo struggle with?
InVideo is less suited for:
High-end realistic avatars
Lifelike presenter-led training videos
Deep multilingual production with automated translation
Highly expressive digital acting
Structured corporate slide-based workflows
InVideo’s strength is creative automation across the timeline rather than focused avatar performance.
What are InVideo’s strengths?
AI Agent for automated video generation
Creative and flexible timeline editing
Scene layout automation from prompt
Quick repurposing workflows
Subtitle and clipping tools
Hybrid generative/manual controls
What are InVideo’s weaknesses?
Avatar realism is limited
Voices are functional, not expressive
No integrated translation workflow
Minimal gesture or motion refinement
Not optimized for presenter-like video ADC
How does InVideo compare to other AI avatar generators?
InVideo operates in a different space than strict avatar studios — it blends automation and editing.
How does InVideo compare to HeyGen?
HeyGen produces expressive and realistic digital presenters with strong voice control and dedicated avatar pipelines. InVideo produces broader video automation with functional avatars as one component. HeyGen outperforms in presenter quality; InVideo excels in creative automation and timeline control.
How does InVideo compare to Synthesia?
Synthesia focuses on structured corporate talkers with seamless multilingual translation and strong presenter realism. InVideo focuses on AI-assisted editing and creative workflows. Synthesia is stronger for pure avatar production; InVideo is stronger for creative, narrative video assembly.
How does InVideo compare to VEED AI?
VEED and InVideo share timeline editing and AI tools, but VEED is more traditional editor-first with added AI features, while InVideo leans more into agent-driven automation. VEED may feel more predictable for manual control; InVideo feels more like an AI collaborator guiding production.
What is the verdict on InVideo?
From my February 2026 testing, InVideo is a capable AI-assisted video production platform where avatars play a supporting role within a broader automation ecosystem.
If your goal is creative automated editing, social content scaling, and hybrid workflows that combine AI-generated structure with manual control, it performs well. If you want
high-realism AI avatars or deeply expressive presenter-led videos
, dedicated avatar studios deliver stronger results.
11. Vyond
URL:
https://www.vyond.com/
What is Vyond?
I tested Vyond in February 2026 on its standard plan. From the start, it was immediately clear that this is not a typical AI avatar platform focused on lifelike digital presenters. Rather, Vyond is an animation-first video creation studio where customizable characters and animated scenes are central.
The interface is built around a timeline and a library of pre-animated assets. Users add scenes, choose character styles, animate actions, and compose the narrative through drag-and-drop storyboarding. There isn’t a traditional AI “script-to-talking-head” workflow here. Instead, Vyond helps you craft animated storytelling pieces with expressive cartoon figures.
During my time in the editor, I found the learning curve steeper than simple avatar generators, but the potential for narrative control and visual variety is greater once you adapt.
How realistic are Vyond’s avatars?
Vyond’s characters are intentionally stylized rather than photorealistic. I did not treat them as digital doubles or synthetic humans — that is not the product’s intent.
Characters look like high-quality 2D or 3D illustrations with smooth, professional animation. The realism in motion comes from pre-defined gesture packs, walk cycles, and emotion tags. You can achieve expressive sequences, but they do not simulate real human faces or natural subtleties.
If your definition of “avatar” is a digital animated persona rather than a lifelike person, Vyond fits. In the context of AI video avatars, however, its output feels more like animation toward storytelling than synthetic people.
How expressive and natural are the avatars?
Expressiveness in Vyond is controlled through manual animation triggers. Characters respond to emotion tags like “happy,” “surprised,” “thoughtful,” or “assertive,” and layered expressions help convey narrative intent.
That said, expressiveness is less fluid than trained AI avatar engines. Movements are not generated from speech patterns — they are driven by timeline events and animation controls you assign manually.
This means the natural quality of the performances depends heavily on how well you structure the scene timings. A character can look animated and engaging, but it won’t have the subtle micro-expressions present in AI-generated presenters.
How good are the voices and lip-sync?
Vyond integrates text-to-speech for character narration and dialogue, but voice quality is neutral and functional rather than emotionally rich. Lip-sync is tied to the platform’s animation engine rather than AI mouth generation.
For basic narration or character dialogue, lip-sync remains serviceable, but it lacks the advanced alignment and emotive inflection seen in Avatar-first platforms. If your project requires strong character voice acting or deep emotional delivery, you might find the built-in voices limited.
The strength of Vyond in this area is not realism, but flexibility — you can manually adjust timing, insert pauses, or swap audio tracks to refine delivery.
How strong is localization and multilingual support?
Multilingual support exists through TTS voices and subtitle generation. You can produce content in multiple languages, and the timeline editor handles text layers and captions effectively.
However, there is no in-editor translation workflow that automatically translates the script and regenerates localized voices in the same process the way more dedicated AI avatar platforms handle it.
Localization works, but it is a manual process that requires setting language and voice parameters yourself for each version.
What use cases does Vyond excel at?
Based on my testing:
Animated storytelling
Explainer videos
Training scenarios with illustrative characters
Internal communications with narrative animation
Projects requiring visual metaphors or symbolic scenes
What use cases does Vyond struggle with?
Vyond is less suited for:
Realistic digital presenters or lifelike avatars
Projects centered on human speech performance
Single-take “talking head” AI video generation
Multilingual corporate voiceovers without manual setup
What are Vyond’s strengths?
Powerful animation timeline editor
Rich library of assets and scene templates
Manual control over gestures and character performance
Effective for explainer and narrative storytelling
Strong support for animated captions and scene sequencing
What are Vyond’s weaknesses?
Not designed for lifelike AI avatars
Voices and lip-sync are functional rather than advanced
Manual animation control required
Localization is manual, not automatic
Less appropriate for corporate talking-head video workflows
How does Vyond compare to other AI avatar generators?
Vyond sits in a different genre compared to classic avatar platforms.
How does Vyond compare to Synthesia?
Synthesia focuses on realistic synthetic presenters with strong multilingual translation and easy script-to-video workflows. Vyond focuses on animated characters and manual scene construction. Synthesia is faster for corporate talking-head videos; Vyond excels in visual storytelling.
How does Vyond compare to HeyGen?
HeyGen delivers expressive, lifelike AI avatars with strong emotional and performance nuance. Vyond delivers composed animated characters driven by scene control rather than AI generation. HeyGen is better for realistic training or marketing videos; Vyond is better for animated narratives.
How does Vyond compare to VEED AI?
VEED integrates avatars within a broader editing and AI generation suite. Vyond is animation-first with deeper manual storytelling controls. If you want editing flexibility with conventional AI avatars, VEED is stronger. If you want illustrative narrative scenes, Vyond outperforms.
What is the verdict on Vyond?
From my February 2026 testing, Vyond is not an avatar generator in the traditional sense — it is an animation studio with character performance controls.
If your goal is animated storytelling, explainer videos, or narrative training modules, Vyond delivers strong creative control and professional results. If your goal is realistic AI presenters, expressive digital actors, or automated multilingual videos, platforms built around AI avatar generation outperform Vyond.

I’ve spent my whole career working in video, and even I find it hard to keep up with how fast AI video is evolving.
To find out which AI video generators are worth your time, I’ve personally tested a range of the leading tools for both cinematic and practical use cases.
My ranking of the best AI video generators
Best AI video generators for cinematic videos
Below is my list of the 12 best AI video models for
creative AI video projects
.
Check out the video below
to quickly see them compared side by side with the same prompt, or read on for my full review of each tool.

How I test cinematic AI video generators
I ran the same set of prompts through each of the cinematic AI video generators to generate a fair comparison.
My test prompt
"A cinematic aerial shot of a floating city above glowing clouds at golden hour. The camera follows a cloaked traveler riding a hovering speeder, weaving between crystal towers suspended in the air.
Below, rivers of light flow between floating islands with waterfalls pouring into mist. Airships drift past in the background, their metallic hulls reflecting sunlight and lens flare. Magic runes flicker on tower surfaces as drones circle.
The traveler's cape ripples in the wind while the camera performs a smooth tracking orbit with natural motion blur and shallow depth of field. Soft volumetric rays pierce through the clouds, creating prismatic reflections.
Hyper-realistic textures (metal, glass, fog), cinematic teal-orange color grading, and a warm, atmospheric tone."
My evaluation criteria
Once the tools had generated a video based on my prompt, I used these criteria to assess the outcome and make my judgments:
Accuracy
: Whether the video correctly follows the prompt, without missing any elements or adding hallucinations
Realism
: How believable the visuals and physics are of the video content, including lighting, textures, and motion
Consistency
: If the objects, motion, and details hold together in a stable way across frames
Creativity
: How the tool interprets the prompt to make it more interesting or engaging
Audio quality
: If the sound is clean and synced to the video content
Performance
: How long the tool took to generate the video and how streamlined the user experience was
‍
Constraints
: If there were limitations around clip length, cost, access, and other factors

My experience
Pros
Veo 3's
output feels cinematic, detailed, and visually polished
. It's one of the strongest AI video models available.
The model offers
very high prompt accuracy
. That means that the videos it generated tended to follow what I asked for in my prompt very closely without many instances of hallucinations.
Veo 3's
integrated audio is really strong
. In my example you can hear the noise of the speeder and some epic-sounding music. Throughout my testing I found that the Veo 3 audio was clean and well-synced.
Cons
Veo 3 is
quite expensive to use
, with a higher cost per clip compared to most of the other models on this list.
The
max clip length of 6 to 8 seconds
is on the shorter end of the range you see across other AI video models, which can be a pain as it limits storytelling flexibility in cases where a longer shot would be ideal.
Veo 3's
camera motion often feels a bit restrained
and less dynamic. In my test I asked for a "smooth tracking orbit", but I didn't really get it.
My verdict
Veo 3 is definitely one of the best AI video generation models available. It offers users cinematic, detailed, and visually rich outputs alongside audio that is context-aware and works together with the visuals in a really impressive way.
I recommend Veo 3 for filmmakers, storytellers, and designers working on premium narrative or branded visuals who don't mind paying extra for quality.

My experience
Pros
ByteDance's model has extremely

and motion dynamics which feel intentional and film-like. I'd say that the camera motion is one of the major advantages of Seedance 2 compared to Veo 3.
Seedance 2 allows you to
generate clips up to 15 seconds
in length which I think is a big advantage. Seedance's
video generation time is also one of the fastest
of any model on this list.
Seedance's
built-in audio is high-quality
and creates immersive sounds with both environmental and musical audio layers.
The model offers one of the
best physics simulations
of any AI video generator on my list too. Again, I'd say it's probably comparable to Veo 3.
Cons
Seedance 2 is still a very new model, so most of the downsides are related to access and pricing. At the time of writing, there's
no reliable way to get free access
.
If you're OK with paying, then I'd suggest using one of the AI video model aggregators I cover later in this post, but that's still a
relatively expensive option
.
Video resolution is
limited to a maximum of 720p
, which can hold back your videos in terms of output quality.
I also found that the
prompt adherence was sometimes a bit sensitive
and inconsistent, and that it felt like my prompts were being interpreted rather than being treated as instructions to strictly follow.
Whenever prompt adherence is an issue the end result is that you need
more generations to get exactly what you want
, which makes the model even more expensive to use.
My verdict
Seedance 2 is pretty amazing and in my opinion is the best model available right now. The model particularly excels in motion, camera intelligence, and realism, and in my opinion is much closer to true cinematic AI video production than any of the other models on this list.
If you're interested in making AI videos for storytelling, film concepts, or high-end visual work, then I highly recommend trying out Seedance 2.
Despite it currently being a pain to get access and the resolution limitations, I'm expecting this model to be regarded as the market leader once it becomes widely available. Of course, there could be another new model that comes out and changes that.

My experience
Pros
I tested Gemini Omni via Google Flow.
The model is very fast
- I generated this 10 second test clip within 1 minute.
Omni
automatically generates multi-shot sequences
like the one you can see in my test output above. It does a good job of selecting the shots and definitely makes the video feel more cinematic.
The model maintains
strong scene consistency
across these different cuts, with the character, environment, and lighting all holding correctly across the different shots.
After generation you can iterate on your video by chatting with the conversational editor and providing additional image and video references. This ability to
progressively refine your scenes
is Omni’s main strength.
I’d recommend trying
Omni as an editing layer
on top of videos you generate in Seedance or Veo.
Cons
While testing Gemini Omni I found that
fast moving objects (especially drones) still deformed
and smeared during rapid movement - you can see it in my test output. I could most likely have fixed this easily, but my rule with these test outputs is to give you my first generation with no edits.
While I really liked the automatic multi-shot sequencing, the feature naturally means that
your manual camera control is limited
. The model decides the cuts rather than you the user, which could be a problem on some video projects.
I had quite a lot of trouble with my prompt being rejected, which gave me the impression that
Omni’s content moderation might be a little heavy-handed
. My test prompt worked on the other models without any issue.
My verdict
Gemini Omni provides users with a really great AI-powered editing environment, but I think in terms of pure output quality it sits below Seedance and Veo.
Since Seedance and Veo produce stronger output, I’d use Omni as an AI-powered editor rather than a standalone generator.

This has resulted in a model with

that followed the instructions in my prompt accurately with minimal deviation.
I really liked how Kling 3 handled my test, and the output really highlights the strengths of the model when it comes to
realistic lighting, physics, and environmental behavior
. The motion, reflections, and clouds all feel grounded.
The
camera motion in Kling 3 is great
and close to Seedance 2 in terms of quality.
Kling 3 also offers a
max video length of 15 seconds
, which is also in line with Seedance 2 and much longer than Veo 3.
Kling 3 also offers some pretty cool
multi-shot workflows
that add production-level control which power users will probably enjoy.
Cons
My main gripe with Kling 3 is that the amazing prompt adherence does come with a downside. I found that the latest model produces output that is slightly
less creatively unpredictable
than other models or earlier versions of Kling.
In some cases that's a good thing, but sometimes the little bits of interpretation that a model does adds color to a video, and I do sometimes think Kling 3
could benefit with being a little bit more experimental
with its interpretation of my prompt.
Aside from that, I found that some complex moving objects (e.g. drones) can still result in
minor distortions in video generation
.
Kling 3 is also
a bit slow when it comes to video generation time
.
My verdict
Kling 3 prioritizes control, consistency, and usability over raw creative randomness, and I think that makes it a very useful model and a strong choice if you want predictable and cinematic results that you can actually build a project around.
Overall, I'd say Seedance 2, Veo 3, and Kling 3 make up my three favorite and most utilized AI video models, and when you combine them you can handle pretty much any creative AI video project you can think of.

My experience
Pros
Runway's strongest feature is its
camera motion
. You can direct the camera to take a wide range of shots and they all look
smooth and cinematic
.
Runway is quite different to the other models we've looked at so far in this list, in that a lot of its value comes from the creative ecosystem that Runway has built around it. The model offers
upscaling, restyling, scene expansion, and workflow chaining.
These are all tools for more advanced users, but the Runway
interface is also clean and intuitive for beginners
.
I think Runway is probably best suited for users who want a strong creative platform with
editing tools and advanced workflows
.
Cons
Runway
doesn't offer built-in audio generation natively in video output
. It does offer built-in tools for audio, voice and SFX, which offer more room for customization and tweaking to get the audio you want, but that also means additional steps to get a video with sound which less advanced users would probably rather avoid.
I found that
Runway's physics is pretty average
compared to the top competitors on this list, and I also noticed a lot of
blur and distortion during motion
. I think you can see some of that come through in my test output above.
My verdict
Runway 4.5 feels like more of a creative experimentation platform than a production-ready AI video generation tool. I think it's a strong platform for ideation, but that it struggles with realism and consistency when it comes to actually generating the final video output. To put it simply, I think Veo, Seedance, and Kling are all much better at generating videos that I want to watch.
I see Runway as a useful toolkit as part of a broader AI video generation workflow, but not very useful as a primary video generation tool. If you are a filmmaker or creative director looking to explore visual concepts, or if camera movement and composition matter more for your project than realism, then Runway might also be a good option for you.

Luma's Ray3 model

Luma's Dream Machine interface itself is
beautiful and intuitive
. I think it's one of the best-designed AI video tools available, and it offers a variety of customization options including camera controls, presets, and start/end frames.
I also liked the Modify editor and Boards features, which I think are useful additions in terms of

I found the Ray3 model to be pretty

You can see in my test above that Luma Ray3
struggled with complex motion and fast-moving scenes
. The physics also appears to break down during moments of dynamic camera movement. While the above video you see is my first generation, this wasn't an isolated incident.
While I found the model aesthetically impressive,
any complex motions seem to get messy
often and objects often got blended together unnaturally.
My verdict
Luma is a fun tool to use, and the Ray3 model does well for certain scenes. I recommend giving it a try if you are trying to generate scenes where atmosphere, elegance and visual storytelling are your priority. It's a much better fit for slower, artistic scenes, but is definitely not suited for action-heavy, dialogue-driven, or realism-critical projects.

The

and I particularly liked the camera movement (see my test output above), which I found to be dynamic, engaging, and really helped to add energy to my scenes.
The city in my test scene felt larger and more impressive than I’d intended, which I think
helps create a cinematic sense of scale
.
The model also has

that did a good job of matching the mood of my scenes.
PixVerse is also a very practical model in that it has both

which includes generous free credit allowances.
The model also offers a

, which goes a long way to helping reduce costs when you're iterating on a video (I wish all AI video generation models had this feature). I also found PixVerse to be very easy to use, and definitely more accessible than some of the higher-end models I mention further up the list.
Cons
The main weakness of PixVerse is the
very short maximum clip duration of only 6 seconds
, which I found very limiting when I was looking to generate something with more depth or complex storytelling. Obviously you can stitch clips together but it still limits the kind of shots you can create.
PixVerse does offer built-in audio generation when generating video, but the
audio quality felt a bit noisy and less polished
than some of the other options on this list, like Seedance or Veo for example.
Another issue I noticed on a few occasions was the
loss of detail and stability whenever I tried a fast camera movement
.
More generally I'd also say that the
realism and fine details are just a bit more limited
compared to the other top-tier models on this list.
My verdict
I think that PixVerse is worth using as a complementary tool, rather than as your primary video generator.
It prioritizes speed, accessibility, and visual impact over realism and depth. I don't think it's very suitable for long-form storytelling or high-end film work, but it is great for quick experiments, ads, and viral-style videos.
I could also see a place for it as a tool for short-form, social-first video content.

The model offers

In general Grok Imagine's
physics and motion consistency can be unreliable
, especially when compared to the top-tier models. I also noticed some occasional loss of fine detail and visual sharpness.
My verdict
Grok Imagine is a highly creative, imagination-first video generator rather than a realism-focused tool. I think it's one of the more interesting tools available right now.
As a result, it's great for emotional storytelling, mood, and visual experimentation, but not ideal for video projects where realism and/or prompt adherence is critical.
I think it's best used during ideation, but after you've got your concept it's best to move to other more controllable tools.

Wan isn't a high-end cinematic model, but it is highly practical and dependable. It's a model that prioritizes usability and flexibility over realism and polish, and I think it excels as a "workhorse" generator when other models might fail due to content moderation restrictions.
